name: OrangeTee & Tie
summary: Property agency network active across condo and landed rentals and sales — negotiate tenant-side fees in writing and confirm stamp-duty reimbursement timing.
body: Agents are not interchangeable — interview for neighbourhood fluency, landlord relationships, and LOI discipline. OrangeTee is one of several large brands; chemistry with your individual agent matters more than logo. If you engage them as your tenant agent, document commission and renewal terms in a CEA prescribed agreement before the first viewing, and clarify that stamp-duty collection is reimbursement after stamping, not a pre-stamp cash grab. Listings that say ‘agent fees apply’ while the salesperson also represents the landlord are a dual-commission / dual-representation risk — confirm engagement in writing and use CEA’s complaint path if needed. Ask for prior cleaning receipts if the TA mandates professional / curtain cleaning, and who pays pest treatment discovered in the first 30 days. If you are comparing rent vs buy, ask for a written cash-flow sketch that includes ABSD (or FTA remission) rather than a mortgage-only spreadsheet. Landed listings for foreigners often have approval caveats — confirm eligibility before emotional deposits. Ask for travel-time honesty to specific campuses at peak hour, not “near Orchard schools” marketing — placement consultants and agents are different vendors with different failure modes.
whenToEngage: Need CEA prescribed agreement before viewings
Purchase / ABSD maths must be stated on OTP
Listing claims tenant fee while agent also represents landlord
Need cleaning / pest / defect-free clauses clarified at LOI
Need peak-hour commute check to named campuses
